New read-only normalized switch/router operational tables over enrolled catalogue templates. Local FortiGate interface/LLDP and applicable MAC tables do not require a serial; managed_switch selects FortiSwitch tables and remains required for interface_errors and port_vlan.
New read-only FortiOS flow triage from route, policy and enrolled session reads.
New optional read-only FortiOS Wi-Fi REST AP/radio inventory.
New optional read-only FortiOS Wi-Fi REST client inventory.
New optional read-only FortiOS Wi-Fi REST rogue AP observations.

New read-only Wi-Fi client event correlation with optional REST signal and observer-scoped neighbor evidence; full compact history pages use history_limit/history_offset and next with a 48000-byte complete structured result bound. REST triage reserves 15 reads.
Doctor supports explicit local-only checks and distinguishes unverified remote readiness.

The description names the canonical CIDR prefixes that the sessions and flow recipes accept inside an enrolled lookup_prefixes entry. The input schema publishes the widest bounds of the recipes, count 1-50, timeout 1-60 and max_bytes 1000-16384, with the bounds per recipe in each description; the Helper checks the bounds of the named recipe and names the field in -32602, so session_list and persistence_list now accept count 9-50 and the FortiADC log recipes 9-20, which a shared limit of 8 refused. The default timeout changes from 5 to 10 seconds, allowing FortiADC nslookup to complete a cold DNS cache lookup; the description documents the new default.
The input schema publishes the existing count limit 1-8 as minimum and maximum; the accepted values are unchanged.
The input schema publishes the existing limits of offset (0-8000000) and max_bytes (1000-48000) as minimum and maximum, so a client can check them before the call; accepted values are unchanged.

target_rate_limits reports the per-target triage sublimit (triage_rate_limit) next to the total rate_limit.

target_scope adds fortios_wifi_rest_enrolled (whether a read-only Wi-Fi REST token is enrolled), fortios_rest_port (effective management HTTPS port, default 443), and triage_rate_limit (the triage sublimit of the total rate_limit).

The catalogue grows to 547 templates (IOS/IOS XE, NX-OS, EOS, Junos, EXOS and FortiOS Wi-Fi reads, plus EXOS vlan_detail and opt-in lag_summary (show sharing) for LAG table reads, IOS/IOS XE interfaces_counters_errors IOS/IOS XE interfaces_details, FortiOS system_interfaces and the three FortiSwitch port/VLAN reads for the switch_read tables); the FortiOS route and policy lookup parameters take the kinds ipv4_lookup/ipv6_lookup (an enrolled address or a prefix inside lookup_prefixes) with updated descriptions; total and catalog_sha256 follow.
Device rows add coverage with inherent and actionable gaps and the incomplete state; audit identity, findings and rule statuses are unchanged.
